c. 1922, September 27
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
(Refused by Catholic News, but printed in the Irish World.)
New York City
To the Editor, Catholic News:
With the earnest appeal of the late Pope Pius X regarding an efficient . Catholic Press, fresh in memory; and with the honest efforts of able pub- lishers before our eyes; and in view of a secular press everywhere, that in general, makes nothing of confusing fact with fiction, ready at any time to cater to Passion and "Bitterly hostile to Justice and Truth", it is surely not without regret that one sees in pages labeled "Catholic", indications of dependence on sources of thought, positively atheistic -- not to say mani- festations of docile servility to dictations of news Agencies, responsible for their existence to that one power, of all powers on earth internation- ally hated as the most prolific source of crime and injustice.
Your present correspondent hardly believes that you wish your, other- wise esteemed little weekly to be a Publication of any such pages. In fact he is confident that you are not conscious of its ever leaving the Press as such, -- and this, notwithstand hisses which he tried to frownaway at a re- cent mass meeting, mostly Catholic, when the Catholic News was mentioned. Nevertheless, he wishes for the general good to call your attention to the fact, that, occasionally at least, you do give out pages indicating such said independence.
As a proof of this contention he would ask you to review, just your own Editorial: "A SANE VIEN OF IRELAND", in your issue of August 5th; or again your Editorial of August 26th: "ASAD BLOW FOR IRELAND." Let us consider this latter, first.
From the very beginning, and throughout, a weakness, sadly common even among our honest Editors, manifests itself. You show, namely, what might be quite excusable in an ordinary reader, a regrettable one-sidedness of infor- mation. With the above-referred to Agencies you seem to espouse views of the situation in Ireland, which Britain would like very much to "believe personally" to be the only proper views. Please just glance it over, and ask yourself if such an article might not be expected rather in a London Daily, or in any of our Metropolitan Yellow Jackets -- every one of them heart and soul in sympathy, not with a crucified Nation or with Catholic Principle, but with Brazen Brutal Britain.
Now it is not the object of this correspondent to discuss the merits or the demerits of the treaty-proffered "Free State", or that of its pro- moters and founders -- one time acknowledged Champions of the Republic which now they seem to have given their lives to suppress. I will only say this just now, in favor of the same or against them; if Britain is in favor of the said "Free State" - and she seems to mightily so-then, honest, an- selfish, lovers of Ireland, and of truth, and of justice, ought to be opposed to it. Why? Because as centuries of Britain-broken Treaties, and British hypocrisy make manifest - the English government or the people composing it cannot be honestly or unselfishly interested in Ireland. Consequently if your correspondent knew absolutely nothing of the claims or the aims of any
